telegramCommands.purpose: Show the same orientation and command list as /help.
Show deterministic commands that remain available if the local model is offline.
Explain Telegram message retention, local-model use, location rounding, and chat authorization.
Prepare one actual-dose candidate without using the language model.
telegramCommands.confirmation: Review the medication, amount, unit, route, and time, then press Confirm. Nothing is recorded before confirmation.

telegramCommands.purpose: Prepare one symptom candidate without using the language model.
telegramCommands.confirmation: Review the symptom, severity, and time, then press Confirm. Nothing is recorded before confirmation.

telegramCommands.purpose: Prepare a paired blood-pressure reading in mmHg with an optional measured pulse.
telegramCommands.confirmation: Review both pressure values, optional pulse, and experienced time, then press Confirm. HealthCurve records the reading without interpreting it.

telegramCommands.purpose: Prepare a body-weight reading while preserving the unit you entered.
telegramCommands.confirmation: Review the value, unit, and experienced time, then press Confirm. Nothing is recorded before confirmation.

telegramCommands.example: /beads-add add a feature that allows me to record hydration
telegramCommands.purpose: Queue a product idea in the fixed HealthCurve feature inbox for a later normal agent run.
telegramCommands.confirmation: The bot returns a queue ID first, then the host bridge returns the hc-* issue ID. Text is treated as untrusted data; no agent, shell command, or implementation starts. Do not include personal health values or secrets.

telegramCommands.purpose: Rapidly record that an emergency injection was given using the injectable medication already configured in HealthCurve.
telegramCommands.confirmation: This safety-critical shortcut records immediately and then reminds you to contact emergency services. It is a record, not an instruction to inject.

telegramCommands.purpose: Open or close a stress episode so related facts can be reviewed together.
telegramCommands.confirmation: The command records the episode state immediately. It does not approve or recommend any dose.

telegramCommands.purpose: Compare what is recorded today with the active physician-approved plan.
telegramCommands.confirmation: No data is created. “Not recorded” never means a zero dose or proves that a dose was missed.

telegramCommands.purpose: Open the optional phone-location flow for the pending draft.
telegramCommands.confirmation: Use Telegram’s share button. Exact coordinates are rounded before storage, and the rounded context is recorded only when the original draft is confirmed.

telegramCommands.purpose: Correct a dose candidate while it is still a pending draft.
telegramCommands.confirmation: Editing does not record anything. Review the updated draft and press Confirm.
Nothing from the cancelled draft becomes a recorded fact.

apiWorkflows.title: Record a scheduled dose from Today
apiWorkflows.instructions: Choose “Record … taken now” beside a scheduled slot. The plan remains unchanged.
apiWorkflows.example: Synthetic example: record the displayed 10 mg hydrocortisone slot at the current time.
apiWorkflows.confirmation: The button itself is the direct entry action; review the displayed plan slot before selecting it.

apiWorkflows.title: Correct a recorded dose
apiWorkflows.instructions: Open a dose, choose Correct recorded fact, change the relevant fields, and provide a reason.
apiWorkflows.example: Synthetic example: correct the experienced time from 07:15 to 07:05 and explain the transcription error.
apiWorkflows.confirmation: Saving creates a new version. The original remains in revision history and is not silently overwritten.

apiWorkflows.title: Correct a recorded symptom
apiWorkflows.instructions: Choose Correct recorded symptom, edit the fields, and provide a correction reason.
apiWorkflows.example: Synthetic example: change nausea severity from 5 to 4 after reviewing the original note.
apiWorkflows.confirmation: Saving preserves the superseded symptom in revision history.

apiWorkflows.title: Open and update a stress episode
apiWorkflows.instructions: Record the trigger, experienced start time, timezone, and optional context. Close it when the episode ends.
apiWorkflows.example: Synthetic example: trigger “stomach illness,” moderate severity, starting 2026-08-01 09:30 America/New_York.
apiWorkflows.confirmation: Web submission records what happened. It never changes the approved plan or recommends an up-dose.

apiWorkflows.title: Record an emergency injection
apiWorkflows.instructions: Use the authenticated emergency page’s fast form, or the deterministic /injection command.
apiWorkflows.example: Synthetic example: record 100 mg of the configured intramuscular medication after it was given.
apiWorkflows.confirmation: This records an event; it does not tell you whether to inject. Follow dated physician-authored instructions and contact emergency services.

apiWorkflows.title: Add location, timezone, and weather context
apiWorkflows.instructions: Use Settings & privacy. Coarse location is the default; exact coordinates require explicit per-record consent.
apiWorkflows.example: Synthetic example: “Synthetic Cambridge,” 2026-08-01 08:30 America/New_York, with optional manual weather.
apiWorkflows.confirmation: Review precision and consent before submitting. Context remains separate from medical facts and can be deleted independently.

apiWorkflows.title: Add facts through the authenticated API
apiWorkflows.availability: API only—no complete web create form yet
apiWorkflows.instructions: Authenticate first and include the in-memory CSRF token on writes. Use explicit local time and IANA timezone.
apiWorkflows.confirmation: API writes are direct user entries. Validate the response; AI output must never call these fact endpoints directly.

importWorkflows.title: Enter a lab panel manually
importWorkflows.availability: API only—web review form is planned
importWorkflows.instructions: Submit original analyte labels, values, units, ranges, specimen time, and source metadata without normalizing them yourself.
importWorkflows.example: Synthetic panel: sodium 140 mmol/L, source range 135–145, collected 2026-08-01 08:00 America/New_York.
importWorkflows.result: Recorded lab facts, with optional separate curated derivations visible on Labs
importWorkflows.confirmation: Manual API entry is direct. Preserve the source report wording and do not infer missing ranges or collection times. HealthCurve derives only allow-listed CBC, acute chemistry, and cortisol values; it never overwrites the source.

importWorkflows.title: Import laboratory CSV
importWorkflows.instructions: Upload to preview first. Review every mapped row and the preview token, then call confirm.
importWorkflows.confirmation: Preview writes no lab facts. The explicit confirm request records only the reviewed rows.

importWorkflows.title: Upload a laboratory PDF
importWorkflows.availability: API upload and extraction review; fact-confirmation UI is planned
importWorkflows.instructions: Upload the PDF into quarantine. Validation and local extraction produce evidence-linked candidates only.
importWorkflows.result: Private source document and confirmation-required AI draft
importWorkflows.confirmation: Uploading or extracting never creates a lab fact. Values and units require explicit review and confirmation in the future review flow.

importWorkflows.title: Import an exported Garmin FIT, CSV, or ZIP file
importWorkflows.availability: API preview and confirm—Garmin account sync is not implemented
importWorkflows.instructions: Upload a provider export for a preview, inspect observed and genuinely missing metrics, then confirm the exact preview.
importWorkflows.confirmation: Preview writes no Garmin facts. Confirm is explicit and idempotent; unavailable metrics remain missing, never zero.
